brief: Systematic investors cut equity exposure sharply last week after the midterm-election volatility spike. Risk Control funds fell to their lowest level in a year, down from the 69th percentile; CTAs turned net short for the first time since March, in the 5th percentile. Combined with leveraged-ETF selling, this produced $365bn of excess sell flow, the largest on record. Hedge funds bought Momentum/Quality and Hyperscalers into Wednesday's rally, then reversed, selling 6:1 into Thursday's drop and cutting gross exposure to the 25th percentile; the AI complex and Tech fell to their lowest exposure levels year to date, with sector-level Tech at the 8th percentile. Friday and Monday showed signs of re-risking starting. UBS argues this de-risking has removed near-term supply just as demand is building: composite managers remain underweight, buyback blackouts are ending (~$50bn next week), retail flows have improved, and foreign investors turned net buyers. Conclusion: near-term risk/reward for US equities is increasingly skewed to the upside into CPI, NVDA earnings, NFP and FOMC.
